title: Principal thickening section lifting
statement: Let R be any commutative ring and W any open of Spec R [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], g in R, and c a natural number. Assume H^1(W,O_W) is subsingleton and g^c kills every element of R killed by any power of g. For f:R -> R/(g), form the principal open thickenings and consecutive transitions [lem-sbc-finite-etale-adic-sections-transfer]. Every section at level n+c restricts to the image of an ambient section of W at level n, for every n. This holds for any family res satisfying identity at gap zero and recursion by the consecutive transitions. No locality, Noetherianity or puncture assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Put F=O_W and j=n+1. Localization is exact, so the scalar torsion bound holds on F. For T=ker(g^(j+c):F->F), C=[F/T --g^(j+c)--> F] is quasi-isomorphic to Q_(j+c)=F/g^(j+c)F. The bound makes g^c:F/T->F well-defined. Together with identity on F it defines C->E_j=[F --g^j--> F]. Composing with E_j->Q_j gives the quotient restriction Q_(j+c)->Q_j. This is the explicit shifted-index inverse construction in Stacks 0H3D, used in 0H3E.

Apply derived global sections to that factorization. The multiplication triangle and the assumed H^1(W,F)=0 identify H^0(RGamma(E_j)) with Gamma(W,F)/g^j Gamma(W,F). Thus the restricted section comes from Gamma(W,F). No depth-three vanishing theorem or Noetherian hypothesis is used here.

ker(R->R/(g))=(g), whose jth power is (g^j). The pullback thickening at n has pushforward structure sheaf F/g^(n+1)F. Under these canonical identifications its maps are the quotient maps; induction using the two recursion laws identifies res with their composites.

lean.statement:
theorem principal_thickening_sections_lift
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (g : R) (W : (Spec (.of R)).Opens)
    (hH : Subsingleton (Modules.H (X := W.toScheme)
      (SheafOfModules.unit W.toScheme.ringCatSheaf) 1))
    (c : ℕ)
    (hkill : ∀ (j : ℕ) (s : R), g ^ j * s = 0 → g ^ c * s = 0) :
    let f := Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {g})
    ∀ (res : ∀ n k : ℕ, Γ(FiniteEtale.Adic.openThickening f W (n + k), ⊤) →
        Γ(FiniteEtale.Adic.openThickening f W n, ⊤)),
      (∀ n t, res n 0 t = t) →
      (∀ n k t, res n (k + 1) t = res n k
        ((FiniteEtale.Adic.openThickeningTransition f W (n + k)).appTop t)) →
      ∀ n (t : Γ(FiniteEtale.Adic.openThickening f W (n + c), ⊤)),
        ∃ a : Γ(W.toScheme, ⊤),
          (FiniteEtale.Adic.openThickeningMap f W n).appTop a = res n c t
